title.narrative: Miracle Millets: Promoting millets for health, climate resilience and rural livelihoods

description.narrative: Direct target groups:(a) 5,000 smallholder farmers, mostly belonging to marginalized communities(b) 200,000 consumers, including both urban and rural consumers.(c) 20 ecopreneurs(d) 30 government officials from the Ministry of Agriculture, Ministry of Women and Child Welfare, MPs and MLAs are being trained to facilitate the promotion of millet through mainstream programmes.(e) 300 Ministry of Agriculture extension workers(f) 1,200 staff members of the Ministry of Women and Child Protection and the Ministry of Education are trained in preparing millet to support the school feeding programme.Institutional direct target groups:(a) Four farmer producer organisations (FPOs)(b) Policy makers and government institutions(c) Millet mission in Chhattisgarh; initiate similar mission in Punjab and MP(d) Networks and alliances:Indirect target group:(a) 22,500 family members of farmers belonging to the direct target group will indirectly benefit from the capacity building and farmer-to-farmer information dissemination programmes.(b) 300 services will reach 150,000 farmers through their capacity building services(c) 12,000 children are reached indirectly through the promotion of millet in the school feeding programme(d) 100,000 additional urban/semi-urban/rural consumers

Millet, being a superfood will full of nutrient and climate friendly in nature, it is critical to create an enabling environment to support and promote millet value chain. This project, will support smallholder farmers from three states of India to apply sustainable production technology in Millet production and connect urban market through farmer institution and ecoprenuers.

Overall objective: Smallholder farmers in three Indian states have increased their food and nutrition security, improved natural resource management and strengthened their resilience to climate change.Project goal: Smallholder farmers in three Indian states are adopting sustainable production methods for millets, urban and rural consumers are better informed about the nutritional, environmental and health benefits of millets, and the policy framework for millets is strengthened.
